stage0_decisions.why_first_mode: ARTEX needs durable graph state plus compare-and-set claim/lease semantics; the repository already has a PostgreSQL-backed repository layer and connection discipline that make the first testable write path realistic without inventing a third store
stage0_decisions.authoritative_backend_for_first_pass: PostgreSQL via the existing argus-workers/database repository pattern
stage0_decisions.attack_graph_relationship: separate; attack_graph_db.py is not repurposed as the exploration graph
stage0_decisions.c18_means_for_artrex_first_pass: one dispatcher-owned graph repository interface; workers/agents return structured output and never commit graph state directly; first tests prove that boundary with a real repository call path

anchors_and_coverage.title: Canonical shared asset graph — anchors and coverage
anchors_and_coverage.reference_behaviour: Each canonical asset can carry engagement-scoped anchor handles and coverage metadata; engagements read and reference the canonical graph through anchors, not by copying subgraphs.
anchors_and_coverage.test_proof: UNIT TESTS EXIST FOR DISPATCHER VALIDATION; INTEGRATION TEST BLOCKED IN THIS ENVIRONMENT
anchors_and_coverage.runtime_proof: NOT RUN (no reachable PostgreSQL in this environment)
anchors_and_coverage.notes: Anchor scopes and coverage metadata are committed on top of the canonical anchor table. Coverage is queried from the perspective of one engagement scope through graph_anchor_scopes, not by copying subgraphs.

per_engagement_exploration_graph.title: Per-engagement exploration graph
per_engagement_exploration_graph.reference_behaviour: An engagement explores by pulling a frontier from the canonical graph into its own exploration space; exploration nodes and edges are traceable back to the canonical node(s) they derive from.
per_engagement_exploration_graph.test_proof: UNIT TESTS EXIST FOR DISPATCHER VALIDATION; INTEGRATION TEST BLOCKED IN THIS ENVIRONMENT
per_engagement_exploration_graph.runtime_proof: NOT RUN (no reachable PostgreSQL in this environment)
per_engagement_exploration_graph.notes: Per-engagement exploration edges are committed and separate from canonical anchors. They describe how an engagement links exploration nodes to each other, traceable back to the canonical node(s) they derive from.

planner_frontier.title: Planner frontier
planner_frontier.reference_behaviour: A recoverable planner frontier per engagement holds the set of canonical/exploration nodes available to the planner for next expansion; frontier state is recoverable from the graph and todo/plan state, not held only in memory.
planner_frontier.test_proof: UNIT TESTS EXIST FOR DISPATCHER VALIDATION; INTEGRATION TEST BLOCKED IN THIS ENVIRONMENT
planner_frontier.runtime_proof: NOT RUN (no reachable PostgreSQL in this environment)
planner_frontier.notes: The frontier is committed as durable per-engagement rows, not in-memory state. Frontier UPSERT/clear/remove/read are implemented in the dispatcher-owned repository path.

persistent_todos.title: Persistent todos
persistent_todos.reference_behaviour: A planner todo store persists planning tasks across restarts; todo items reference engagements, canonical nodes, exploration nodes, frontier position, and status, with status transitions open/in-progress/done/blocked.
persistent_todos.test_proof: UNIT TESTS EXIST FOR DISPATCHER VALIDATION; INTEGRATION TEST BLOCKED IN THIS ENVIRONMENT
persistent_todos.runtime_proof: NOT RUN (no reachable PostgreSQL in this environment)
persistent_todos.notes: Todos are the durable representation of planner work. Status transitions set started_at/completed_at appropriately and go through the dispatcher-owned repository path.

graph_outbox.title: Graph outbox
graph_outbox.reference_behaviour: Graph-side changes can be staged onto a dispatcher-owned outbox and dequeued for downstream consumers with at-least-once handling basics and a clear dispatcher ownership boundary.
graph_outbox.test_proof: UNIT TESTS EXIST FOR DISPATCHER VALIDATION; INTEGRATION TEST BLOCKED IN THIS ENVIRONMENT
graph_outbox.runtime_proof: NOT RUN (no reachable PostgreSQL in this environment)
graph_outbox.notes: The outbox is dispatcher-owned. Dequeued rows are marked dequeued and timestamped but not deleted, so downstream consumers can reconcile against the outbox. Error recording and requeue are provided.

graph_change_driven_planning.title: Graph-change-driven planning
graph_change_driven_planning.reference_behaviour: Graph mutations (canonical or exploration) can trigger planning consideration through the outbox/frontier rather than polling; the flow is graph change -> outbox event -> planner frontier/todo update -> next planning pass, with the planner able to recompute from persisted state on restart.
